_readme: Hand-built mapping from Elite Dangerous journal identifiers to Elite Explorer's own Guardian site-type enum. Sourced independently from the public journal manual (https://elite-journal.readthedocs.io/), our own CodexEntry cross-checks, and cross-referenced against the journalName field returned by Canonn's public /gstypes and /grtypes endpoints (docs.canonn.tech) to confirm which $Ancient_* prefix belongs to which site category. Not derived from any third-party tool's source — Canonn's *data* (their public API response) is not GPL, only their server software is. Extend only from things we've verified ourselves.
_note_ruins: Guardian Ruins (Alpha/Beta/Gamma 'broken ground' sites) all share the bare $Ancient journal Name with no size/layout suffix — Canonn's own /grtypes table confirms this by listing an empty journalName for every ruin type. That means the journal alone cannot tell us WHICH ruin layout we're at, only that it's a ruin; matching a specific layout requires cross-referencing our recorded lat/long origin against Canonn's site data for that system.
_note_structures: Guardian Structures DO encode their specific layout in the journal Name (the _NNN suffix under Tiny/Small/Medium), and Canonn's /gstypes table gives us the human-readable name for each. Listed here as a courtesy cross-reference — not required for our own siteType classification, which only needs the size prefix.

codexFallback.note: Used only to confirm/fill origin lat-long when ApproachSettlement wasn't seen; Name_Localised is stored as a secondary label, not used for siteType classification since it's a display string that can be ambiguous across ruin sizes.
